To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of the four diastereomers of trans-2-(ter-butoxycarbonylethylaminomethyl)-pyrrolidinyl acetic acids has been accomplished.

the trans-L-2-(terbutoxycarbamylaminomethyl)- 4-(thyminyl)pyrrolidinyl acetic acid PNA monomer binds DNA in a sequence-specific manner with a binding affinity similar to that observed for the natural L-PNA monomer.
the synthesis of trans-2-(tertbutoxycarbonlyamino methyl)-4-(thymino 1-yl)pyrrolidin 1-yl acetics acids was achieved and the binding of these PNAs to DNA/RNA was investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, synthesis and characterization of a new class of PNA oligomers, which contain the pyrrolidine backbone and are capable of binding to complementary DNA and RNA sequences with high selectivity.
the development of a new class of PNAs that are capable of binding to DNA/RNA with high affinity and specificity and that are capable of forming stable triplexes and G-quartet structures.
the synthesis of stereoisomeric pyrrolidine-based PNAs and their complexation properties with DNA/RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L- and D-PNA oligomers are equally effective in DNA recognition and the stereoisomerism at the pyrrolidine ring has a negligible effect on binding.
the binding preferences of PNAs with complementary nucleic acids is highly dependent on the stereochemical nature of the PNA monomer.
PNAs containing the L- or D-pyrrolidine monomer are able to form stable complexes with complementary RNA, but not with DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L/D-PNA monomer 2,3,4-tri-tert-butylpyrrole (I) can be prepared by a straightforward synthetic route.
the binding affinity of PNA oligomer with DNA is not dependent upon the stereochemistry of pyrrolidine backbone, however, a slight preference for L-PNA was noted in the case of DNA/RNA heteroduplex.
PNAs are capable of binding to DNA/RNA in a sequence specific fashion, and the binding affinity of PNAs can be modulated by changing the stereochemical configuration of the side chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trans-configuration of the pyrrolidine backbone is essential for the formation of stable duplexes with DNA and that the L and D isomers have comparable DNA binding properties.
the trans-L/D- 2-(tert- butoxycarbonyl amino-methyl)-4-(thymine-1-yl)-pyrrolidinyl acetic acid monomer is a suitable candidate for the development of a PNA that can bind to both DNA and RNA.
the binding preferences of PNAs with complementary RNA are dictated by the stereochemistry of the pyrrolidine backbone.
